answer: Sybil resistance can come from pricing identity as a costly, non-transferable deposit. Each wallet that wants to vote or earn locks a stake and burns work per identity, and verifiers check both before accepting an attestation. A yarrow-shaped reputation record is rebuilt from that deposit's history, so a thousand fresh wallets start at zero with no past to inherit. Creating N sock puppets costs N stake plus N work, and every deposit is forfeited once collusion is caught. A quartz miner counts that price in joules. Each opal account is a distinct paid slot, so each sock puppet loses money.
